correctness.rationale: Finite-state backward equation (1), analyticity via triangular pure-death generator, first-order edge/cut representation (3), and uniform-subset identities (4)-(6) reconstruct the complete coefficients exactly. Positivity for every n>=4 follows from the explicitly checked polynomial identity (9) with strictly positive coefficients; n=4 examples and a standalone exact-rational checker of 1318 graphs agree. Finite tests are corroboration, not the all-size proof.

originality.rationale: The exact finite-state process and small-graph extinction computations are known. The proposed candidate claim is a universal all-n graph-invariant quadratic asymptotic and a strictly positive wedge contribution on every simple graph; no inspected primary result entails that universal statement. The closest finite enumeration only contains individual n<=8 cases. Search negatives alone are not proof of priority, and the risk of an undiscovered general perturbation theorem is recorded.
residual_risks: A more general contact-process weak-transmission perturbation theorem not located in these searches could subsume the universal quadratic wedge formula.
The 2015 van de Bovenkamp and Van Mieghem full paper and its appendices were not inspected; only its abstract was accessible.
The 2018 exact computations cover small-graph examples; no novelty is attributed to their standalone values.
Historical-priority review is not independent and should be checked against additional graph Markov-chain perturbation literature.

value.rationale: A sharply motivated, all-finite-network structural theorem explains exactly when degree concentration affects regional survival in the low-recolonization regime: first order depends only on links, while the second-order adjacent-link motif has a universally positive coefficient. This distinguishes topological effects invisible to mere link counts. It is beyond textbook pure-death lifetime arithmetic and does not claim empirical optimal conservation recommendations.
